It seems every other week, a streaming service raises its prices. This week, ESPN announced price increases for both ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited, along with adjustments to some Disney+ and Hulu bundles.

This round of price hikes was uncovered by the sports media tracking site Sports Media Watch through ESPN's support page, with the new rates set to take effect on September 17. Here are the details:

  • ESPN Select monthly fee: $14 per month (previously $13 per month)
  • ESPN Select annual fee: $140 per year (previously $130 per year)
  • ESPN Unlimited monthly fee: $32 per month (previously $30 per month)
  • ESPN Unlimited annual fee: $320 per year (previously $300 per year)

As the report notes, this marks the first price adjustment for these services since ESPN overhauled its streaming strategy last year.

Meanwhile, the prices of certain Disney bundles are also going up in line with ESPN's streaming increases.

  • Disney+ (with ads), Hulu (with ads) and ESPN Select bundle: $22 per month (previously $20 per month)
  • Disney+ (no ads), Hulu (no ads) and ESPN Select bundle: $33 per month (previously $30 per month)

As pointed out by The Verge, the price hike also affects an older no-ads Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Select bundle that is no longer available to new subscribers, with its monthly fee rising from $25 to $28.

It is worth noting that ESPN Unlimited bundle plans are not affected by this round of price adjustments.

Last week, Peacock announced price increases for some of its plans, with monthly hikes of up to $3 or annual hikes of up to $30. Apple also recently raised prices for Apple Music and Apple One.
